translations.text: The judgment against Nineveh, in the book of the visions of Nahum the Elkoshite.
The Lord is a jealous and avenging God. The Lord takes vengeance in anger. The Lord takes vengeance on those who hate him and holds his anger against his enemies.
The Lord is slow to anger and great in power, and he certainly does not acquit the guilty. The Lord's way is in the whirlwind and the storm, and the clouds are the dust beneath his feet.
He rebukes the sea and dries it up, and he dries up all the rivers. Bashan and Carmel mourn, and the growth of Lebanon withers.
The mountains quake before him, and the hills dissolve. The earth trembles before him—the world and all its inhabitants.
Who can stand before his anger? Who can endure his fierce wrath? His wrath burns like fire, and the mountains melt before him.
The Lord is good, giving help in the day of distress, and he knows those who trust in him.
With a flood he brings complete destruction; he will sweep through its place, and darkness will pursue his enemies.
What are you plotting against the Lord? He brings complete destruction, and distress will not arise twice.
For even their rulers are rebellious, and they are drunk in their drunkenness. They have eaten and filled themselves with dry stubble.
From you will come someone who plots evil against the Lord and devises injustice.
Thus says the Lord concerning the heads of the many waters that flowed and passed away: Though I afflicted you, I will not afflict you again.
Now I will break his yoke from you and cut your bonds.
The Lord will issue a command against you: No more offspring bearing your name will be sown. In the house of your god I will destroy the carved and cast images, and I will soon make it your grave.

Look! On the mountains are the feet of the one who brings good news and announces peace. Judah, celebrate your festivals and fulfill your vows, for the wicked one will no longer act against you, because he has been utterly destroyed.
A leader has come up before you. He keeps watch, watches the road, braces his waist, and is very strong in power.
For I am restoring the glory of Jacob like the glory of Israel, because threshers have threshed them and ruined their vine branches.
The shields of their warriors are red, and the mighty men play with flaming torches and with chariots on the day they prepare themselves. The horsemen are bewildered.
They boast of their name in their chariots and show off. Their appearance is like torches, and they race like lightning.
They will seize their rulers and stumble as they walk. They will hurry to the wall and prepare [?].
The gates of Judah were opened, and the palace shook.
She stationed her horsemen and went up, while her slave women moaned in their hearts like doves.
Nineveh is like a pool of water; she is a reservoir. Yet they are fleeing. “Stop! Stop!” But no one turns back.
Plunder the silver! Plunder the gold! There is no end to her adornments; all her precious vessels are strong.
Threshed, overthrown, and shattered! Hearts are broken, knees buckle, and every waist trembles. All their faces have turned black like soot on a pot.
Where is the lioness's den and the feeding place of the lioness's cub, where the lion used to go in, along with the lion's cub, with no one to frighten them?
The lion tore apart enough food for his cubs and cut up prey for his mates as well. He filled his caves and his den with torn prey.

Look, I am against you, says the mighty Lord. I will destroy your troops in smoke, and the sword will devour your cubs. I will remove your prey from the earth, and the voice of your servants will no longer be heard.
Woe to the city of blood, entirely deceitful and full of injustice! Plunder never leaves it.
The crack of the whip, the sound of rattling wheels, a galloping horse, and a bouncing chariot!
A charging horseman, a gleaming sword, and a flashing spear! A multitude of slain, a mass of corpses! There is no end to the corpses; they stumble over their bodies.
Because of the many acts of prostitution of the beautiful prostitute, the mistress of sorcery, who raises nations through her prostitution and clans through her sorcery.
Look, I am against you, says the mighty Lord. I will lift your skirts over your face and show your nakedness to the nations and your shame to the kingdoms.
I will throw filth on you, disgrace you, and make you a spectacle.
Everyone who sees you will flee from you and say, “Nineveh has been plundered! Who will grieve for you?” Where shall I look for someone to comfort you?
Are you better than No-amon, which sits among rivers, surrounded by water, whose strength is the sea and whose wall is water?
Cush and Egypt were her strength, without limit. The people of Put and Libya were her helpers.
She too went into captivity. Her little children were dashed to pieces at the corners of all her streets. They cast lots for her honored people, and all her nobles were bound in chains.
You too will become sick and be despised. You too will seek help against your enemies.
All your fortresses are like fig trees with early figs: when they ripen, they fall into the eater’s mouth.
Your people within you are like women. The gates of your land will be opened to your enemies, and fire will devour your bars.
Store up water for yourself for the siege and strengthen your fortresses. Go into the mud, tread the clay, and strengthen the [?].
There fire will devour you, and the sword will destroy you. It will devour you like the caterpillar, because you have grown strong like the caterpillar and numerous like the locust.
You have multiplied your merchants far beyond the stars of heaven. The locust plunders and flies away.
Your princes are like locusts, and your warriors like locusts clinging to a hedge on a cold day. When the sun rises, they fly away, and no one knows where they are.
Your companions, the kings of Assyria, have fallen asleep, and your close associates have lain down. Your people are scattered over the mountains, with no one to gather them.
No one grieves over your ruin; your wound is painful. All who have heard news of you clap their hands over you, because your wickedness has continually swept over everyone.
